chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Zurara, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He is free (to perform the prayer) if he is detained, whether he makes a stipulation or not.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prayer if one is detained during Ihram without making a stipulation?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi underscores the principle of ease (yusr) in Shia jurisprudence, affirming that involuntary detention nullifies the requirement for explicit stipulation (shart) during prayer. It highlights the scholarly consensus that the validity of the prayer depends on the actual impediment rather than the ritualistic declaration, reflecting the broader legal maxim that compulsion removes obligation.
